passages.note: Campaign page in the third person ("Steve will extend the $500 limit to the Legislature"); even as his words, a pay-to-play cap on lobbying interests is a narrow limit, not a strict limit on corporate or dark-money spending, so it shows only the pro-limit side.
Opposition to Proposition 4 and public campaign financing concerns taxpayer money, not how much private political money is limited, and is written in the third person.
Describes PG&E donations and uncapped behested payments as corruption but proposes no campaign-finance rule; the plan section is about utilities.
Discusses his own fundraising totals and donor count, which is conduct, not a rule for money in campaigns.

rows.reasoning: The only on-question passage, "Steve will extend the $500 limit to the Legislature", is the campaign's third-person promise, not his own words, so nothing survives V1. Even in his own words, a pay-to-play cap on contributions from lobbying interests would not match "Strictly limit corporate and dark-money spending" (a narrow ban is direction-only), and opposing Proposition 4 public financing is off the private-money axis.
